###  <::after> 🌊 Reimagine real-time data engineering. 

📚 [ **Documentation** ](https://docs.risingwave.com/) 🚀 [ **Slack Community** ](https://risingwave.com/slack)

[ ](https://risingwave.com/slack) [ ](https://x.com/risingwavelabs) [ ](https://www.youtube.com/@risingwave-labs)

RisingWave is a Postgres-compatible SQL database engineered to provide the _**simplest** _ and _**most cost-efficient** _ approach for **processing** , **analyzing** , and **managing** real-time event streaming data. 

RisingWave can **ingest** millions of events per second, continuously **join and analyze** live data streams with historical tables, **serve** ad-hoc queries in real-time, and **deliver** fresh, consistent results wherever needed. 

[ ](/root/risingwave/-/raw/main/docs/dev/src/images/architecture_20240908.png)

##  <::after> Try it out in 60 seconds 

Install RisingWave standalone mode: 
    
    
    curl https://risingwave.com/sh | sh

To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see [ Quick Start ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/get-started/) . 

##  <::after> When is RisingWave the perfect fit? 

RisingWave is the ideal solution for: 

  * <::marker>Managing real-time data sources like Kafka streams, database CDC, and more. 
  * <::marker>Executing complex, on-the-fly queries, including joins, aggregations, and time windowing. 
  * <::marker>Interactively and concurrently exploring consistent, up-to-the-moment results. 
  * <::marker>Seamlessly delivering results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker>Processing both streaming and batch data with a unified codebase. 



##  <::after> In what use cases does RisingWave excel? 

RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases: 

  * <::marker> **Streaming analytics** : Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring. 
  * <::marker> **Event-driven applications** : Develop sophisticated monitoring and alerting systems for critical applications such as fraud and anomaly detection. 
  * <::marker> **Real-time data enrichment** : Continuously ingest data from diverse sources, conduct real-time data enrichment, and efficiently deliver the results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker> **Feature engineering** : Transform batch and streaming data into features in your machine learning models using a unified codebase, ensuring seamless integration and consistency. 



##  <::after> Production deployments 

[ **RisingWave Cloud** ](https://cloud.risingwave.com) offers the easiest way to run RisingWave in production. 

For **Docker deployment** , please refer to [ Docker Compose ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-docker-compose/) . 

For **Kubernetes deployment** , please refer to [ Kubernetes with Helm ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-k8s-helm/) or [ Kubernetes with Operator ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-kubernetes/) . 

##  <::after> Community 

Looking for help, discussions, collaboration opportunities, or a casual afternoon chat with our fellow engineers and community members? Join our [ Slack workspace ](https://risingwave.com/slack) ! 

##  <::after> Notes on telemetry 

RisingWave uses [ Scarf ](https://scarf.sh/) to collect anonymized installation analytics. These analytics help support us understand and improve the distribution of our package. The privacy policy of Scarf is available at [ https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy ](https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy) . 

RisingWave also collects anonymous usage statistics to better understand how the community is using RisingWave. The sole intention of this exercise is to help improve the product. Users may opt out easily at any time. Please refer to the [ user documentation ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/telemetry/) for more details. 

##  <::after> License 

RisingWave is distributed under the Apache License (Version 2.0). Please refer to [ LICENSE ](/root/risingwave/-/blob/main/LICENSE) for more information. 

##  <::after> Contributing 

Thanks for your interest in contributing to the project! Please refer to [ RisingWave Developer Guide ](https://risingwavelabs.github.io/risingwave/) for more information.

###  <::after> 🌊 Reimagine real-time data engineering. 

📚 [ **Documentation** ](https://docs.risingwave.com/) 🚀 [ **Slack Community** ](https://risingwave.com/slack)

[ ](https://risingwave.com/slack) [ ](https://x.com/risingwavelabs) [ ](https://www.youtube.com/@risingwave-labs)

RisingWave is a Postgres-compatible SQL database engineered to provide the _**simplest** _ and _**most cost-efficient** _ approach for **processing** , **analyzing** , and **managing** real-time event streaming data. 

RisingWave can **ingest** millions of events per second, continuously **join and analyze** live data streams with historical tables, **serve** ad-hoc queries in real-time, and **deliver** fresh, consistent results wherever needed. 

[ ](/root/risingwave/-/raw/main/docs/dev/src/images/architecture_20240908.png)

##  <::after> Try it out in 60 seconds 

Install RisingWave standalone mode: 
    
    
    curl https://risingwave.com/sh | sh

To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see [ Quick Start ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/get-started/) . 

##  <::after> When is RisingWave the perfect fit? 

RisingWave is the ideal solution for: 

  * <::marker>Managing real-time data sources like Kafka streams, database CDC, and more. 
  * <::marker>Executing complex, on-the-fly queries, including joins, aggregations, and time windowing. 
  * <::marker>Interactively and concurrently exploring consistent, up-to-the-moment results. 
  * <::marker>Seamlessly delivering results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker>Processing both streaming and batch data with a unified codebase. 



##  <::after> In what use cases does RisingWave excel? 

RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases: 

  * <::marker> **Streaming analytics** : Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring. 
  * <::marker> **Event-driven applications** : Develop sophisticated monitoring and alerting systems for critical applications such as fraud and anomaly detection. 
  * <::marker> **Real-time data enrichment** : Continuously ingest data from diverse sources, conduct real-time data enrichment, and efficiently deliver the results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker> **Feature engineering** : Transform batch and streaming data into features in your machine learning models using a unified codebase, ensuring seamless integration and consistency. 



##  <::after> Production deployments 

[ **RisingWave Cloud** ](https://cloud.risingwave.com) offers the easiest way to run RisingWave in production. 

For **Docker deployment** , please refer to [ Docker Compose ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-docker-compose/) . 

For **Kubernetes deployment** , please refer to [ Kubernetes with Helm ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-k8s-helm/) or [ Kubernetes with Operator ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-kubernetes/) . 

##  <::after> Community 

Looking for help, discussions, collaboration opportunities, or a casual afternoon chat with our fellow engineers and community members? Join our [ Slack workspace ](https://risingwave.com/slack) ! 

##  <::after> Notes on telemetry 

RisingWave uses [ Scarf ](https://scarf.sh/) to collect anonymized installation analytics. These analytics help support us understand and improve the distribution of our package. The privacy policy of Scarf is available at [ https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy ](https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy) . 

RisingWave also collects anonymous usage statistics to better understand how the community is using RisingWave. The sole intention of this exercise is to help improve the product. Users may opt out easily at any time. Please refer to the [ user documentation ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/telemetry/) for more details. 

##  <::after> License 

RisingWave is distributed under the Apache License (Version 2.0). Please refer to [ LICENSE ](/root/risingwave/-/blob/main/LICENSE) for more information. 

##  <::after> Contributing 

Thanks for your interest in contributing to the project! Please refer to [ RisingWave Developer Guide ](https://risingwavelabs.github.io/risingwave/) for more information.

###  <::after> 🌊 Reimagine real-time data engineering. 

📚 [ **Documentation** ](https://docs.risingwave.com/) 🚀 [ **Slack Community** ](https://risingwave.com/slack)

[ ](https://risingwave.com/slack) [ ](https://x.com/risingwavelabs) [ ](https://www.youtube.com/@risingwave-labs)

RisingWave is a Postgres-compatible SQL database engineered to provide the _**simplest** _ and _**most cost-efficient** _ approach for **processing** , **analyzing** , and **managing** real-time event streaming data. 

RisingWave can **ingest** millions of events per second, continuously **join and analyze** live data streams with historical tables, **serve** ad-hoc queries in real-time, and **deliver** fresh, consistent results wherever needed. 

[ ](/root/risingwave/-/raw/main/docs/dev/src/images/architecture_20240908.png)

##  <::after> Try it out in 60 seconds 

Install RisingWave standalone mode: 
    
    
    curl https://risingwave.com/sh | sh

To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see [ Quick Start ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/get-started/) . 

##  <::after> When is RisingWave the perfect fit? 

RisingWave is the ideal solution for: 

  * <::marker>Managing real-time data sources like Kafka streams, database CDC, and more. 
  * <::marker>Executing complex, on-the-fly queries, including joins, aggregations, and time windowing. 
  * <::marker>Interactively and concurrently exploring consistent, up-to-the-moment results. 
  * <::marker>Seamlessly delivering results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker>Processing both streaming and batch data with a unified codebase. 



##  <::after> In what use cases does RisingWave excel? 

RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases: 

  * <::marker> **Streaming analytics** : Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring. 
  * <::marker> **Event-driven applications** : Develop sophisticated monitoring and alerting systems for critical applications such as fraud and anomaly detection. 
  * <::marker> **Real-time data enrichment** : Continuously ingest data from diverse sources, conduct real-time data enrichment, and efficiently deliver the results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker> **Feature engineering** : Transform batch and streaming data into features in your machine learning models using a unified codebase, ensuring seamless integration and consistency. 



##  <::after> Production deployments 

[ **RisingWave Cloud** ](https://cloud.risingwave.com) offers the easiest way to run RisingWave in production. 

For **Docker deployment** , please refer to [ Docker Compose ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-docker-compose/) . 

For **Kubernetes deployment** , please refer to [ Kubernetes with Helm ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-k8s-helm/) or [ Kubernetes with Operator ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-kubernetes/) . 

##  <::after> Community 

Looking for help, discussions, collaboration opportunities, or a casual afternoon chat with our fellow engineers and community members? Join our [ Slack workspace ](https://risingwave.com/slack) ! 

##  <::after> Notes on telemetry 

RisingWave uses [ Scarf ](https://scarf.sh/) to collect anonymized installation analytics. These analytics help support us understand and improve the distribution of our package. The privacy policy of Scarf is available at [ https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy ](https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy) . 

RisingWave also collects anonymous usage statistics to better understand how the community is using RisingWave. The sole intention of this exercise is to help improve the product. Users may opt out easily at any time. Please refer to the [ user documentation ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/telemetry/) for more details. 

##  <::after> License 

RisingWave is distributed under the Apache License (Version 2.0). Please refer to [ LICENSE ](/root/risingwave/-/blob/main/LICENSE) for more information. 

##  <::after> Contributing 

Thanks for your interest in contributing to the project! Please refer to [ RisingWave Developer Guide ](https://risingwavelabs.github.io/risingwave/) for more information.

###  <::after> 🌊 Reimagine real-time data engineering. 

📚 [ **Documentation** ](https://docs.risingwave.com/) 🚀 [ **Slack Community** ](https://risingwave.com/slack)

[ ](https://risingwave.com/slack) [ ](https://x.com/risingwavelabs) [ ](https://www.youtube.com/@risingwave-labs)

RisingWave is a Postgres-compatible SQL database engineered to provide the _**simplest** _ and _**most cost-efficient** _ approach for **processing** , **analyzing** , and **managing** real-time event streaming data. 

RisingWave can **ingest** millions of events per second, continuously **join and analyze** live data streams with historical tables, **serve** ad-hoc queries in real-time, and **deliver** fresh, consistent results wherever needed. 

[ ](/root/risingwave/-/raw/main/docs/dev/src/images/architecture_20240908.png)

##  <::after> Try it out in 60 seconds 

Install RisingWave standalone mode: 
    
    
    curl https://risingwave.com/sh | sh

To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see [ Quick Start ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/get-started/) . 

##  <::after> When is RisingWave the perfect fit? 

RisingWave is the ideal solution for: 

  * <::marker>Managing real-time data sources like Kafka streams, database CDC, and more. 
  * <::marker>Executing complex, on-the-fly queries, including joins, aggregations, and time windowing. 
  * <::marker>Interactively and concurrently exploring consistent, up-to-the-moment results. 
  * <::marker>Seamlessly delivering results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker>Processing both streaming and batch data with a unified codebase. 



##  <::after> In what use cases does RisingWave excel? 

RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases: 

  * <::marker> **Streaming analytics** : Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring. 
  * <::marker> **Event-driven applications** : Develop sophisticated monitoring and alerting systems for critical applications such as fraud and anomaly detection. 
  * <::marker> **Real-time data enrichment** : Continuously ingest data from diverse sources, conduct real-time data enrichment, and efficiently deliver the results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker> **Feature engineering** : Transform batch and streaming data into features in your machine learning models using a unified codebase, ensuring seamless integration and consistency. 



##  <::after> Production deployments 

[ **RisingWave Cloud** ](https://cloud.risingwave.com) offers the easiest way to run RisingWave in production. 

For **Docker deployment** , please refer to [ Docker Compose ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-docker-compose/) . 

For **Kubernetes deployment** , please refer to [ Kubernetes with Helm ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-k8s-helm/) or [ Kubernetes with Operator ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-kubernetes/) . 

##  <::after> Community 

Looking for help, discussions, collaboration opportunities, or a casual afternoon chat with our fellow engineers and community members? Join our [ Slack workspace ](https://risingwave.com/slack) ! 

##  <::after> Notes on telemetry 

RisingWave uses [ Scarf ](https://scarf.sh/) to collect anonymized installation analytics. These analytics help support us understand and improve the distribution of our package. The privacy policy of Scarf is available at [ https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy ](https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy) . 

RisingWave also collects anonymous usage statistics to better understand how the community is using RisingWave. The sole intention of this exercise is to help improve the product. Users may opt out easily at any time. Please refer to the [ user documentation ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/telemetry/) for more details.

###  <::after> 🌊 Reimagine real-time data engineering. 

📚 [ **Documentation** ](https://docs.risingwave.com/) 🚀 [ **Slack Community** ](https://risingwave.com/slack)

[ ](https://risingwave.com/slack) [ ](https://x.com/risingwavelabs) [ ](https://www.youtube.com/@risingwave-labs)

RisingWave is a Postgres-compatible SQL database engineered to provide the _**simplest** _ and _**most cost-efficient** _ approach for **processing** , **analyzing** , and **managing** real-time event streaming data. 

RisingWave can **ingest** millions of events per second, continuously **join and analyze** live data streams with historical tables, **serve** ad-hoc queries in real-time, and **deliver** fresh, consistent results wherever needed. 

[ ](/root/risingwave/-/raw/main/docs/dev/src/images/architecture_20240908.png)

##  <::after> Try it out in 60 seconds 

Install RisingWave standalone mode: 
    
    
    curl https://risingwave.com/sh | sh

To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see [ Quick Start ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/get-started/) . 

##  <::after> When is RisingWave the perfect fit? 

RisingWave is the ideal solution for: 

  * <::marker>Managing real-time data sources like Kafka streams, database CDC, and more. 
  * <::marker>Executing complex, on-the-fly queries, including joins, aggregations, and time windowing. 
  * <::marker>Interactively and concurrently exploring consistent, up-to-the-moment results. 
  * <::marker>Seamlessly delivering results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker>Processing both streaming and batch data with a unified codebase. 



##  <::after> In what use cases does RisingWave excel? 

RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases: 

  * <::marker> **Streaming analytics** : Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring. 
  * <::marker> **Event-driven applications** : Develop sophisticated monitoring and alerting systems for critical applications such as fraud and anomaly detection. 
  * <::marker> **Real-time data enrichment** : Continuously ingest data from diverse sources, conduct real-time data enrichment, and efficiently deliver the results to downstream systems. 
  * <::marker> **Feature engineering** : Transform batch and streaming data into features in your machine learning models using a unified codebase, ensuring seamless integration and consistency. 



##  <::after> Production deployments 

[ **RisingWave Cloud** ](https://cloud.risingwave.com) offers the easiest way to run RisingWave in production. 

For **Docker deployment** , please refer to [ Docker Compose ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-docker-compose/) . 

For **Kubernetes deployment** , please refer to [ Kubernetes with Helm ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-k8s-helm/) or [ Kubernetes with Operator ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/risingwave-kubernetes/) . 

##  <::after> Community 

Looking for help, discussions, collaboration opportunities, or a casual afternoon chat with our fellow engineers and community members? Join our [ Slack workspace ](https://risingwave.com/slack) ! 

##  <::after> Notes on telemetry 

RisingWave uses [ Scarf ](https://scarf.sh/) to collect anonymized installation analytics. These analytics help support us understand and improve the distribution of our package. The privacy policy of Scarf is available at [ https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy ](https://about.scarf.sh/privacy-policy) . 

RisingWave also collects anonymous usage statistics to better understand how the community is using RisingWave. The sole intention of this exercise is to help improve the product. Users may opt out easily at any time. Please refer to the [ user documentation ](https://docs.risingwave.com/docs/current/telemetry/) for more details.

docs/dev/src/metrics.md:36:Next, high barrier latency could also be caused by buffers in the graph.
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:37:If some downstream buffer is congested, we will be unable to queue and continue processing upstream messages.
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:41:This means the upstream executor will be unable to continue processing new stream messages, until some space on the buffer is freed.
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:43:The various buffer sizes can currently be adjusted via options in the developer configuration file.
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:44:For instance, options to configure buffer size of the exchange executor can be found [here](https://github.com/risingwavelabs/risingwave/blob/a36e01307d60491b91870ac5a37049a378fe986f/src/config/example.toml#L49-L50).
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:46:Another subtle cause is that large buffer size can also worsen barrier latency.
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:48:Typically, backpressure kicks in, the source is throttled.
docs/dev/src/metrics.md:49:If buffer sizes are too large, or if there are many buffers, there will not be backpressure applied to source immediately.
docs/dev/src/SUMMARY.md:44:    - [Shared Buffer](./design/shared-buffer.md)
docs/dev/src/contributing.md:64:- If there is a conflict, it will open an issue and make the original author the assignee.
docs/dev/src/design/checkpoint.md:12:Internally, the upcoming changes may take a while to propagate from sources to materialized views, and at least one barrier event is required to flush the changes. Such two kinds of latency determine the latency between write and read.
docs/dev/src/design/checkpoint.md:32:   - For other operators, the barrier messages flow through the operators and trigger a checkpoint operation on them. Namely, flush the changes into storage.
docs/dev/src/design/checkpoint.md:33:3. When all dirty states from a compute node are flushed to storage, the compute node sends a finish signal to the meta service.
docs/dev/src/design/checkpoint.md:40:A local shared buffer is introduced to stage these uncommitted write batches. Once the checkpoint barriers have pass through all actors, the storage manager can notify all compute nodes to 'commit' their buffered write batches into the shared storage.
docs/dev/src/design/checkpoint.md:42:![shared buffer](../images/checkpoint/shared-buffer.svg)

docs/dev/src/design/state-store-overview.md:131:Every operation on the LSM-tree yields a new ***version*** on the Hummock manager, e.g., adding new L0 SSTs and compactions. In streaming, each stream barrier is associated with an ***epoch***. When the barrier flows across the system and collected by the stream manager, we can start doing ***checkpoint*** on this epoch. SSTs produced in a single checkpoint are associated with an ***uncommitted epoch***. After all compute nodes flush shared buffers to shared storage, the Hummock manager considers the epoch committed.
